identity.title: ALMA detection of a tentative nearly edge-on rotating disk around the nearby AGB star R Doradus

paper_type_evidence.quote: A spectral scan of the circumstellar environment of the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star R Doradus was taken with ALMA in cycle 2 at frequencies between 335 and 362 GHz

evidence.quote: At a distance of only 59 pc (cite: Knapp2003), R Dor is the nearest AGB star to our Sun.
At a distance of only 59 pc (cite: Knapp2003), R Dor is the nearest AGB star to our Sun.

question.value: Does the spatial offset between blue and red shifted molecular emission in R Dor's inner wind indicate a compact rotating disk, and what are its properties and possible companion?

evidence.quote: we investigate a peculiar feature seen in various molecular transitions of ALMA (cycle 2) Band 7 observations of (hereafter R Dor), which suggest the presence of a compact rotating disk in its inner wind.
R Doradus was observed with ALMA in Band 7 in August and September 2015 (proposal 2013.1.00166.S, PI L. Decin).

analysis_steps.goal: Stereograms of blue vs red emission

method.value: Sum blue and red channels separately about lsr velocity and overplot

evidence.quote: we separate the channels on the blue shifted side of the lsr velocity from the red shifted channels for a given transition, sum the respective emission separately and overplot the results.

analysis_steps.goal: Determine position angle and PV diagrams

method.value: Orthogonal pairs of PV diagrams at 5° intervals through image centre; slit width one resolution element, plus 0.9" wide slit

evidence.quote: we made orthogonal pairs of position-velocity (PV) diagrams with axes at $5^\circ$ intervals through the centre of the image.
The uncertainty on these estimates is $\sim5^\circ$.

method.value: 3D NLTE LIME model of sub-Keplerian disk, passed through CASA observation simulation, compared to PV diagrams

evidence.quote: we aim to reproduce the observed three-dimensional emission distribution by assuming a differentially rotating disk.

analysis_steps.goal: Disk mass, angular momentum, companion mass

method.value: Integrate density over volume; angular momentum assuming conservation; companion mass assuming ~30% transfer efficiency

evidence.quote: Having estimated the disk density, we can calculate its mass (to first order) by integrating over the volume.

findings_qualitative.value: Blue blob lacks HCN and continuum counterpart

evidence.quote: Though HCN emission is strong throughout in the CSE of R Dor, it is, surprisingly, altogether lacking in the blob.

claims.hypothesis: Offset red/blue emission indicates a compact nearly edge-on rotating disk
claims.experiment: PV diagrams of 28SiO v=1 and LIME disk model
claims.result: Model reproduces global PV shape; disk inclined 110°, inner rim 6 AU, 3e-6 Msun
claims.finding: A tentative sub-Keplerian disk is present

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, the overall behaviour is reproduced by the model.

claims.hypothesis: Disk angular momentum requires a companion
claims.experiment: Compare disk angular momentum to stellar one
claims.result: Companion of at least 2.5 Earth masses at 6 AU
claims.finding: Angular momentum problem solved by a planetary companion

evidence.quote: We note that this is a preliminary lower limit estimate

claims.hypothesis: The blue blob is associated with a companion planet

evidence.quote: The current quality of the data does not permit us to confirm or exclude any hypothesis regarding the nature and origin of the blue blob.
